elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: Affiliate assignments remain subject to the general requirement for the other party’s prior written consent; no affiliate exception is included.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The clause generally permits assignment in connection with a merger without consent, but requires consent if the transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party. The preferred right is not subject to that exception.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The clause generally permits assignment in connection with an acquisition without consent, but requires consent if the transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The clause permits assignment in a sale of all or substantially all assets related to the Agreement, but requires consent when the transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party; therefore the right is not unconditional as required.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer’s consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign without Customer consent in connection with Vendor’s merger, acquisition, or qualifying asset sale unless the transaction involves Customer’s direct competitor.

elements.element: Customer’s consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The added qualifier states that the other party’s consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, including when Customer consent to a Vendor assignment is required.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Assignments involving Customer’s direct competitor are subject to Customer consent rather than absolutely prohibited, so Customer could consent to such an assignment.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer’s change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants no termination right in connection with Customer’s change of control or any assignment transaction.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Customer’s successor assignment right is subject to the other party’s consent when the transaction involves that party’s direct competitor.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor’s successor assignment right is subject to Customer consent when the transaction involves Customer’s direct competitor.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning the Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause conditions assignments in connection with a merger, acquisition, or qualifying asset sale on written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning the Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: The same written-notice requirement applies mutually to Vendor’s assignments in connection with a merger, acquisition, or qualifying asset sale.

elements.element: Customer’s assignments other than successor assignments require the other party’s consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires prior written consent for assignments, and the only relevant no-consent exception covers specified successor transactions.

elements.element: The other party may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer’s other assignments.
elements.evidence: The added language provides that consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor’s assignments other than successor assignments require the other party’s consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires prior written consent for assignments, subject to the specified successor-transaction exception.

elements.element: The other party may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor’s other assignments.
elements.evidence: The added language provides that consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The redline adds the fallback’s reasonableness qualifier and written-notice requirement, but it retains the direct-competitor consent carveout for successor transactions. As a result, neither party has the fallback’s complete right to assign to successors on notice without consent. It also does not achieve the preferred position because there is no Customer affiliate exception, Customer successor assignments remain restricted in competitor transactions, Vendor retains no-consent successor-assignment rights, and Vendor assignments to Customer competitors are not absolutely prohibited. The changes otherwise preserve the clause’s unrelated operative terms, but the redline is not minimal toward a complete playbook level because it does not remove the competitor carveout needed to achieve the fallback.
